body:
Closes #37.

## What the issue asked for

> See examples from https://github.com/konard/vk-bot-desktop and github.com/link-assistant/formal-ai on how we automate desktop app releases, docs and user landing pages. We should also try to make full web app in a similar way, yet it may have restricted features, unless local server is started (which should be installable via npm).
>
> We need to collect data related about the issue to this repository, make sure we compile that data to `./docs/case-studies/issue-{id}` folder, and use it to do deep case study analysis (also make sure to search online for additional facts and data), list of each and all requirements from the issue, and propose possible solutions and solution plans for each requirement …

## What this PR adds

The case study lists every requirement (R1–R12), the reference repos and the root causes found along the way: [`docs/case-studies/issue-37/`](https://github.com/link-foundation/meta-sovereign/blob/issue-37-3578e6d14474/docs/case-studies/issue-37/README.md). Options, choices and status per requirement are in [`solution-plan.md`](https://github.com/link-foundation/meta-sovereign/blob/issue-37-3578e6d14474/docs/case-studies/issue-37/solution-plan.md), and online sources in [`external-research.md`](https://github.com/link-foundation/meta-sovereign/blob/issue-37-3578e6d14474/docs/case-studies/issue-37/external-research.md).

- **Desktop apps (R1)** — electron-builder 26 around the existing Electron shell, which already embeds the server:
  - Linux AppImage/deb/tar.gz, macOS dmg/zip, Windows NSIS installer/portable, each for x64 and arm64 (`desktop/electron-builder.config.cjs`, `npm run desktop:build`).
  - `prepare-desktop.mjs` stages a minimal app (built SPA, `electron-updater` as the only dependency); `build-desktop.mjs` resolves the Electron version from npm.
  - The packaged app could not start before: the store lived in the working directory, the start guard waited for a script path in `argv`, which packaged apps do not pass, and electron-updater's CommonJS `autoUpdater` was read wrongly from ESM. All three are fixed in `js/electron/main.js`.
  - App icon from `desktop/icon.svg`.
- **Automated releases (R2)** — `.github/workflows/desktop-release.yml`, the same `workflow_run` pattern as formal-ai:
  - Native runners for each platform, with smoke tests: deb/tar contents on Linux, installer and portable exe on Windows, bundle name, bundle id and `codesign --verify --deep --strict` (also inside each dmg) on macOS.
  - Uploads installers, update feeds, `SHA256SUMS.txt`, `BUILD-PROVENANCE.txt` and `actions/attest` build attestations; `validate-desktop-assets.mjs` checks the set first.
  - macOS: Developer ID + notarization when the five secrets exist, ad-hoc signing otherwise (`mac.identity=-` + `desktop/adhoc-sign-mac.cjs`, as in vk-bot-desktop), so Apple Silicon builds launch after **Open Anyway**.
  - Pull requests dry-run the full matrix without publishing.
  - `desktop-release-gate.mjs`: the release run on `main` currently ends in failure only because `Publish to npm` returns E404 (see below). The desktop build now still runs in that case, and stops on any other failure.
- **Landing page (R4)** — `/download/` on GitHub Pages (`js/src/web/download/`):
  - detects OS and arch, offers the matching installer from the newest release that has desktop assets, lists every other build;
  - checks a downloaded file against `SHA256SUMS.txt` in the browser;
  - falls back to the Releases page; en/ru/zh/hi.
- **Full web app with restricted features (R5–R6)** — the SPA already worked offline, but it could never see a local server from GitHub Pages:
  - **Root cause:** the server sent no CORS headers, so every cross-origin request failed in every browser ([`cors-before.txt`](https://github.com/link-foundation/meta-sovereign/blob/issue-37-3578e6d14474/docs/case-studies/issue-37/verification-logs/cors-before.txt)).
  - `js/src/server/cors.js`: an allow-list (the hosted origin and the Capacitor origins by default), preflights including `Access-Control-Allow-Private-Network`, 403 for unlisted origins on preflight and state-changing requests. Configurable with `serve --allow-origin=<origins|none>` or `MS_ALLOW_ORIGINS`.
  - A **browser-only mode** notice: the `npx` commands to start the server, a **Check again** button that rediscovers the server and reloads into the full app, a link to the download page and a Safari hint.
- **Server via npm (R7)** — the existing `meta-sovereign` package: `npx -y meta-sovereign serve`, with `npx -y github:link-foundation/meta-sovereign serve` until the first npm release.
- **Docs (R3)** — README "Desktop app" section and browser-only mode; USER-GUIDE §3–§5 and troubleshooting (download, first launch on each OS, checksums, CORS, browser notes), all in en/ru/zh/hi. Changeset (minor).

## Maintainer actions

1. **npm first publish.** `meta-sovereign` has never been published, and trusted publishing (OIDC) needs an existing package, so every release run ends in `E404` at `Publish to npm`. Publish once by hand, then add `release.yml` as trusted publisher on npmjs.com.
2. **Optional signing.** Add `MAC_CSC_LINK`, `MAC_CSC_KEY_PASSWORD`, `APPLE_API_KEY`, `APPLE_API_KEY_ID`, `APPLE_API_ISSUER` for signed and notarized macOS builds with auto-update. Without them builds are ad-hoc signed. Windows builds are unsigned (SmartScreen "Run anyway").

## Verification

- `npm test`: 640/640 pass. New tests: `desktop-packaging`, `desktop-downloads`, `desktop-release-gate`, `download-page`, `server-cors`, `web-mode`, `build-pages`, `mobile-electron-packaging`.
- `npm run lint -- --max-warnings 0`, `npm run format:check`, `npx jscpd .` and the file line limits pass.
- CI desktop dry run [38178457136](https://github.com/link-foundation/meta-sovereign/actions/runs/38178457136): Linux x64/arm64, Windows x64/arm64 and macOS builds and smoke tests pass; the macOS apps pass `codesign --verify` ([excerpt](https://github.com/link-foundation/meta-sovereign/blob/issue-37-3578e6d14474/docs/case-studies/issue-37/verification-logs/macos-adhoc-sign.txt)).
- Local Linux x64 build, package check and launch of the packaged app with its embedded server ([logs](https://github.com/link-foundation/meta-sovereign/blob/issue-37-3578e6d14474/docs/case-studies/issue-37/verification-logs/)).
- CORS before/after with a real local server in Chromium, Firefox and WebKit (`experiments/issue-37/hosted-web-local-server.mjs`): on `main` every request fails; with this PR an allow-listed origin succeeds in all three, and an unlisted one is still refused ([`cors-after.txt`](https://github.com/link-foundation/meta-sovereign/blob/issue-37-3578e6d14474/docs/case-studies/issue-37/verification-logs/cors-after.txt)).
- Gate on real runs: main run 38172634346 → `build=true` (only npm failed); desktop run 38176417737 → `build=false`.

![Download page](https://github.com/link-foundation/meta-sovereign/blob/issue-37-3578e6d14474/docs/screenshots/issue-37/download-page-ready.png?raw=true)
![Download page fallback](https://github.com/link-foundation/meta-sovereign/blob/issue-37-3578e6d14474/docs/screenshots/issue-37/download-page-fallback.png?raw=true)
![Download page, Russian, mobile](https://github.com/link-foundation/meta-sovereign/blob/issue-37-3578e6d14474/docs/screenshots/issue-37/download-page-mobile-ru.png?raw=true)

![Browser-only mode](https://github.com/link-foundation/meta-sovereign/blob/issue-37-3578e6d14474/docs/screenshots/issue-37/web-mode-offline.png?raw=true)
![Browser-only mode, Russian, mobile](https://github.com/link-foundation/meta-sovereign/blob/issue-37-3578e6d14474/docs/screenshots/issue-37/web-mode-mobile-ru.png?raw=true)

## Known limits

- The first real desktop release can only run on `main` after merge.
- Safari blocks `https` pages from reaching `http://127.0.0.1` (WebKit bug 171934); Safari users open the server's own page or use the desktop app. Chrome 142+ and newer Firefox ask once for local network access.
- The Rust server still sends `Access-Control-Allow-Origin: *`; porting the allow-list, and WebSocket `Origin` checks, are follow-ups.
- Ad-hoc macOS builds do not auto-update; Windows arm64 has auto-update off.
title: feat(desktop): multi-platform desktop apps, download page and browser-only web mode (#37)
